name: Leadership and People Management
certifications: No formal certification; assessed by role plays, a ninety-day plan and a leadership portfolio
Optional: ILM Level 3 or Level 5 in Leadership and Management
Optional: CMI Level 5 in Management and Leadership
tools: HR system such as Workday or SuccessFactors

beginner.summary: For new and first-time managers, team leads and senior individual contributors stepping into people leadership. Covers the move from doing the work to leading people, the manager's responsibilities, self-awareness, one-to-ones, goals and expectations, delegation, feedback, recognition, team meetings, time management, trust, early underperformance, managing former peers, team communication, hiring, onboarding, team conflict, wellbeing and the HR rules every manager must know.
prerequisites: Newly promoted or about to lead a team, or leads work informally
Has at least two years of work experience
Willing to practise conversations in role plays
outcomes: Run one-to-ones, set goals and delegate work with clear expectations
Give feedback and recognition that change behaviour
Handle early underperformance, conflict and workload problems fairly
Hire, onboard and lead a team within company policy and employment law

days.topic: Leadership and People Management Overview: From Individual Contributor to Manager
subtopics: What changes when you become a manager
Results through others instead of your own work
The common mistakes of new managers
What your team needs from you
Your time: from doing to enabling
Course structure, role plays and the ninety-day plan
days.lab_task: Complete a leadership self-assessment, map how your time will change from individual work to management, interview a manager you respect about their first year and set three goals for this course.
days.deliverable: Self-assessment, time map, interview notes and three goals
checks: The time map shows the shift from doing to enabling
The interview records three lessons from an experienced manager
Three goals are specific and linked to the self-assessment

days.topic: The Manager's Role: Responsibilities, Authority and Expectations
subtopics: Accountabilities for people, results and process
What you can decide and what needs approval
Representing the company to the team
Representing the team to the company
Contracting expectations with your own manager
Working with HR, finance and IT
Writing your role on one page
days.lab_task: Write a one-page description of your role with accountabilities and decision rights, check it with a role-played senior manager and build a RACI for five common team decisions.
days.deliverable: One-page role description and decision RACI
checks: People, results and process accountabilities are listed
Each of the five decisions has one accountable person
The senior manager confirms the role description

days.topic: Knowing Yourself as a Leader: Strengths, Values and Blind Spots
subtopics: Strengths and how they become weaknesses
Preferences in communication and decision style
Blind spots and how to find them
Asking for feedback on your leadership
days.lab_task: Complete a strengths or style profile, ask three colleagues for feedback on how you work under pressure, compare the results and write a one-paragraph leadership statement.
days.deliverable: Profile summary, feedback themes and leadership statement
checks: Three strengths with examples from work are recorded
At least one blind spot is confirmed by colleague feedback
The statement links values to how you will lead
objectives: Define how you want to lead

days.topic: One-to-One Meetings That Matter
subtopics: Why one-to-ones are the manager's most important meeting
Frequency, length and who owns the agenda
When the person has nothing to say
days.lab_task: Run three role-played one-to-ones with different team members (a high performer, a quiet person and someone frustrated), use the question bank and keep notes with actions.
days.deliverable: One-to-one template, notes and actions for three meetings
checks: The team member talks for most of the meeting
Each meeting includes a question beyond task status
Each meeting ends with at least one agreed action

days.topic: Setting Clear Goals and Expectations
subtopics: Linking team goals to company goals
Writing expectations for behaviour, not just output
Agreeing goals rather than imposing them
days.lab_task: Write team OKRs linked to a company goal, agree two individual goals with a role-played team member and set a monthly review rhythm.
days.deliverable: Team OKRs, two agreed individual goals and a review plan
checks: Each team objective links to a company goal
Every key result has a measure and a target
The team member contributes to their goals in the role play

days.topic: Delegating Work: What, to Whom and How Much
subtopics: Why new managers fail to delegate
What to delegate and what to keep
Matching tasks to skill and will
Levels of delegation from tell to empower
days.lab_task: List your current tasks, choose five to delegate, match each to a team member and delegation level, and brief one task in a role play with checkpoints agreed.
days.deliverable: Delegation plan and a recorded task briefing
checks: Five tasks are selected with reasons
Each task has a delegation level suited to the person
The team member restates goal, limits and checkpoints
objectives: Brief and follow up delegated work

days.topic: Giving Feedback as a Manager: SBI and Feedforward
subtopics: Asking for feedback from your team
days.lab_task: Prepare and give one reinforcing and two redirecting pieces of feedback in role plays using SBI, handle a defensive reaction and ask the team member for feedback on your management.
days.deliverable: Three SBI scripts, recordings and a feedback log
checks: Each piece of feedback names situation, behaviour and impact
The defensive role play ends with an agreed next step
The manager asks for and records feedback on themselves

days.topic: Recognition and Motivation
subtopics: Specific recognition compared with general praise
days.lab_task: Find out what motivates each of four role-played team members, write specific recognition for recent work linked to company values and design a recognition habit for the team.
days.deliverable: Motivation notes, recognition messages and a team habit
checks: Motivators are recorded for each team member
Each recognition names the work and its effect
The plan recognises all team members over a quarter

days.topic: Running Team Meetings and Rituals
subtopics: Team meetings that are worth attending
Decisions and actions from team meetings
Cutting meetings that do not work
days.lab_task: Design a team meeting rhythm, run a role-played weekly meeting and a retrospective, and cut or change one meeting based on a meeting health check.
days.deliverable: Team meeting rhythm, meeting notes and health check
checks: Each meeting has a purpose and length
Every participant speaks in the role-played meeting
One meeting is changed or cut based on the health check

days.topic: Managing Time and Priorities as a New Manager
subtopics: Saying no and pushing back upward
days.lab_task: Audit one week of your calendar, classify your activities, redesign the next week to protect one-to-ones and thinking time, and practise pushing back on one request in a role play.
days.deliverable: Calendar audit, redesigned week and push-back script
checks: Activities are classified by type and value
One-to-ones and team time are scheduled first
The push-back keeps the relationship and offers an alternative

days.topic: Building Trust with Your Team
subtopics: Being honest when you cannot share
days.lab_task: Assess trust in a case team, identify the manager behaviours that damaged it, write a trust-repair plan and role-play the first conversation that starts the repair.
days.deliverable: Trust assessment, repair plan and conversation notes
checks: The assessment names behaviours that broke trust
The plan has specific commitments with dates
The role-play conversation admits the problem and states actions

days.topic: Handling Underperformance Early
subtopics: The first conversation about a performance gap
Involving HR at the right time
days.lab_task: Prepare and hold a first conversation with a role-played team member who misses deadlines, agree expectations and support, and write a factual note of the meeting.
days.deliverable: Conversation plan, recording and meeting note
checks: The plan considers skill, will and circumstance
The conversation ends with clear expectations and support
The note records facts without opinions

days.topic: Managing Former Peers and Friends
subtopics: Fairness when friends are on the team
Handling the person who wanted your job
Asking for support from your manager
days.lab_task: Plan and role-play a reset conversation with a former peer, and another with a colleague who applied for your role, then write the boundaries you will keep.
days.deliverable: Two conversation plans, recordings and personal boundaries
checks: The conversation names the change in relationship
The second conversation acknowledges feelings and agrees a way forward
Boundaries cover confidentiality, fairness and social contact

days.topic: Team Communication: Updates, Decisions and Transparency
subtopics: What the team needs to know and when
Explaining decisions you did not make
days.lab_task: Explain an unpopular company decision to a role-played team, answer their questions honestly, and write the follow-up update with the agreed next steps.
days.deliverable: Team briefing notes, Q&A log and written update
checks: The briefing explains the reasons without blaming leadership
Questions you cannot answer are acknowledged with a follow-up date
The team can restate what changes for them

days.topic: Hiring Your First Team Members
subtopics: Defining the role and success profile
days.lab_task: Write a success profile and job description for a role, build a structured interview with scored questions, interview two role-played candidates and make a documented decision.
days.deliverable: Job description, interview kit and decision record
checks: The success profile lists outcomes for the first year
Both candidates are scored on the same questions and scale
The decision is based on scored evidence

days.topic: Onboarding New Team Members
subtopics: The first day and first week
days.lab_task: Build an onboarding plan for a new team member with a pre-boarding checklist, first-week schedule and thirty-sixty-ninety goals, and review it with a role-played new joiner.
days.deliverable: Onboarding plan and checklist
checks: The first week has a day-by-day schedule
Thirty, sixty and ninety-day goals are measurable
A buddy and check-in rhythm are assigned
objectives: Provide support in the first months

days.topic: Conflict Within the Team: Spotting and Resolving It
days.lab_task: Map a conflict between two role-played team members, meet each separately, facilitate a joint conversation that ends in a written agreement and plan the follow-up.
days.deliverable: Conflict map, conversation notes and written agreement
checks: The map identifies the type and causes of conflict
Both parties speak and are heard in the joint conversation
The agreement lists specific behaviours and a review date

days.topic: Managing Wellbeing, Workload and Burnout Signs
subtopics: Looking after yourself as a manager
days.lab_task: Review a team workload tracker, identify two people at risk of overload, hold a wellbeing conversation in a role play and rebalance the work with a documented plan.
days.deliverable: Workload review, conversation notes and rebalance plan
checks: Two people at risk are identified from the tracker
The conversation offers support and referral routes
The plan moves or removes work with agreement

days.topic: HR Basics for Managers: Policies, Leave and Employment Law Essentials
subtopics: Sickness absence and return to work
Harassment and how to respond to complaints
Confidentiality and data protection for employee records
Local labour law differences such as India, the UK and the US
When to call HR before acting
tools: HR system such as Workday or SuccessFactors
days.lab_task: Work through six people-management scenarios (leave, sickness, a harassment complaint, probation, a grievance and a data request), decide what policy applies and what to do first, and check answers with an HR partner.
days.deliverable: Scenario answers with policy references
checks: Each scenario cites the relevant policy
Scenarios needing HR are escalated before action
Employee information is handled within data protection rules

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: First Ninety Days as a Manager Plan
days.lab_task: Build a ninety-day plan for a real or realistic new team, with listening activities, goals, rhythms and early wins, and present it to a role-played senior manager who challenges it.
days.deliverable: Ninety-day plan and presentation
checks: The first month includes one-to-ones and stakeholder meetings
The plan includes measurable goals and early wins
Challenges from the senior manager are answered with reasons
objectives: Present a plan to your manager

intermediate.summary: For managers with one or more years of experience leading a team. Covers situational leadership, coaching with GROW, performance reviews and calibration, performance improvement plans, high-performing teams, psychological safety, motivation, leading change at team level, decision making and bias, conflict between teams, influencing peers and senior leaders, hybrid teams, career conversations, inclusion, capacity planning, budgets, retention, matrix teams and difficult behaviours.
prerequisites: Has led a team for at least a year
Runs one-to-ones and gives feedback regularly
Has completed beginner people management training or has equivalent experience
outcomes: Adapt leadership style and coach people to higher performance
Run fair performance reviews, calibration and improvement plans
Build safe, inclusive and high-performing teams that adapt to change
Influence across the organisation and keep strong people

days.topic: Situational Leadership: Adapting Style to the Person and Task
subtopics: Why one leadership style is not enough
Directing, coaching, supporting and delegating styles
Diagnosing competence and commitment for a task
Agreeing the style openly with the person
days.lab_task: Diagnose four role-played team members on two tasks each, choose a style for each combination and hold two conversations that use different styles, then explain the choices.
days.deliverable: Diagnosis grid and two recorded conversations
checks: Each person and task has a competence and commitment rating
The chosen style fits each diagnosis
The two conversations show clearly different styles

days.topic: Coaching Conversations with the GROW Model
subtopics: Coaching compared with telling and mentoring
Goal, reality, options and way forward
Avoiding the urge to give answers
Coaching for performance and for growth
days.lab_task: Coach a role-played team member through a real work challenge using GROW for twenty minutes, then switch roles, and log the questions that moved the conversation forward.
days.deliverable: Coaching recording and coaching log
checks: All four stages appear in order
The coachee leaves with a specific action and date

days.topic: Performance Reviews and Calibration
subtopics: Common rating biases: recency, halo and similarity
Linking reviews to pay and promotion carefully
tools: HR system such as Workday or SuccessFactors
days.lab_task: Write reviews for three sample employees from evidence logs, take part in a calibration meeting with other managers, adjust ratings with reasons and deliver one review conversation.
days.deliverable: Three written reviews, calibration notes and a recorded review conversation
checks: Every rating is supported by examples
Rating changes in calibration are explained
The conversation covers strengths, gaps and next goals

days.topic: Performance Improvement Plans and Fair Process
subtopics: When an improvement plan is appropriate
Working with HR through the plan
Treating the person with dignity throughout
days.lab_task: Write an improvement plan for a role-played employee with measurable goals, support and review dates, hold the opening meeting and the first review with HR in the room.
days.deliverable: Improvement plan and notes of two meetings
checks: Each goal has a measure and a deadline
The plan lists the support the company will give
Meetings follow the company policy steps

days.topic: Building High-Performing Teams: Roles, Norms and Accountability
subtopics: Fixing a team that is stuck
days.lab_task: Run a team chartering workshop with a role-played team to agree purpose, roles, norms and measures, then run a health check and agree two actions.
days.deliverable: Team charter, health check results and actions
checks: The team purpose is written in one or two sentences
Norms cover meetings, decisions and conflict

days.topic: Psychological Safety in Practice
subtopics: What psychological safety is and is not
Signs a team does not feel safe
How managers make it safe to speak up
Responding to bad news and mistakes
days.lab_task: Measure psychological safety in a case team with a short survey, run a blameless review of a recent mistake and practise responses that encourage people to raise problems.
days.deliverable: Survey results, blameless review and response scripts
checks: Survey results identify the weakest areas
The review focuses on systems and decisions, not people
Response scripts thank people for raising problems
objectives: Keep high standards and safety together

days.topic: Motivation Science: Autonomy, Mastery and Purpose
subtopics: Autonomy: choice in how work is done
days.lab_task: Hold motivation conversations with two role-played team members, identify demotivators in their work and agree job-crafting changes that add autonomy, mastery or purpose.
days.deliverable: Conversation notes and job-crafting agreements
checks: Each conversation identifies at least one demotivator
Each agreement changes something about how the work is done
Each person can state how their work affects customers or the business

days.topic: Leading Through Change at Team Level
subtopics: Explaining the why of a change
Involving the team in how to change
days.lab_task: Lead a role-played team through a process change, explain the reasons, run a session where the team designs how to implement it and handle two resistant team members.
days.deliverable: Change plan, team session notes and conversation notes
checks: The team can state the reason for the change
The implementation plan includes team ideas
Resistant team members agree to a next step

days.topic: Decision Making for Managers: Data, Judgement and Bias
subtopics: Types of decisions and who should make them
Using data without waiting for perfect data
Common biases: confirmation, anchoring and sunk cost
days.lab_task: Make a staffing decision in a case using a decision matrix and bias checklist, consult a role-played team, record the decision and review it against what happened next in the case.
days.deliverable: Decision matrix, decision log entry and review
checks: Options are scored against agreed criteria
At least two biases are checked and addressed
The review compares the decision with the outcome

days.topic: Managing Conflict Between Teams
subtopics: Why teams conflict: goals, resources and handoffs
Protecting your team without blaming others
days.lab_task: Resolve a handoff conflict between two role-played teams by meeting the other manager, running a joint problem-solving session and agreeing a written service agreement.
days.deliverable: Conflict map, workshop notes and service agreement
checks: The map identifies goal, resource or handoff causes
Both teams contribute to the solution
The service agreement has measures and a review date

days.topic: Influencing Peers and Senior Leaders
subtopics: Mapping stakeholders and what they care about
Handling a no from a senior leader
Influencing in meetings and in writing
days.lab_task: Plan how to win support for a team proposal from two peers and a senior leader, hold the three conversations in role plays and adjust the proposal after their objections.
days.deliverable: Influence plan, conversation notes and revised proposal
checks: Each stakeholder's interests and concerns are listed
Each conversation frames the proposal in the stakeholder's terms
The revised proposal answers the objections raised

days.topic: Leading Hybrid and Remote Teams Day to Day
subtopics: Fair treatment of remote and office staff
days.lab_task: Review a hybrid team case where remote staff feel left out, write a team agreement that fixes the causes and run a hybrid meeting that includes remote people equally.
days.deliverable: Case review, team agreement and meeting observation
checks: The review names practices that exclude remote staff
The agreement covers meetings, availability and decisions
Remote participants contribute equally in the meeting

days.topic: Career Conversations and Development Plans
subtopics: What people want from their careers
Development plans with experiences, not only courses
days.lab_task: Hold a career conversation with a role-played team member, build a development plan based mostly on work experiences and give honest feedback on their promotion readiness.
days.deliverable: Career conversation notes and development plan
checks: The notes record the person's goals in their own words
Most development actions are on-the-job experiences
Promotion readiness feedback is specific with gaps named

days.topic: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion for People Managers
subtopics: Fair allocation of work and opportunities
days.lab_task: Audit work allocation and stretch opportunities in a case team for patterns, role-play a response to an exclusionary comment and agree three inclusion actions for the team.
days.deliverable: Allocation audit, response script and inclusion actions
checks: The audit identifies who gets visible work and who does not
The response addresses the comment calmly and clearly
Three inclusion actions have owners and measures

days.topic: Workforce Planning and Team Capacity
subtopics: Skills matrices and single points of failure
days.lab_task: Build a skills matrix and capacity plan for a case team, find single points of failure and a capacity gap, and present options to a role-played stakeholder.
days.deliverable: Skills matrix, capacity plan and options paper
checks: Single points of failure are identified
The capacity gap is stated in people or hours
Options include cost, time and risk

days.topic: Budget and Resource Management for Team Leaders
subtopics: Team budgets: people, tools, training and travel
Explaining budget limits to the team
days.lab_task: Build next year's budget request for a case team, track a quarter of sample spend against it, make two trade-offs when costs rise and explain the changes to the team.
days.deliverable: Budget request, spend tracker and trade-off notes
checks: The request separates people, tools, training and travel
Variances are explained for the quarter
Trade-offs keep spend within budget with reasons

days.topic: Retention: Stay Interviews and Preventing Regretted Attrition
subtopics: Exit interviews that teach you something
days.lab_task: Rate retention risk for a case team, hold a stay interview with a role-played high performer and write a retention plan with actions within your control.
days.deliverable: Retention risk matrix, stay interview notes and retention plan
checks: Each person has a risk and impact rating
The stay interview identifies what would make the person leave
The plan lists actions the manager controls

days.topic: Leading Cross-Functional and Matrix Teams
subtopics: Leading people who do not report to you
days.lab_task: Set up a cross-functional project team in a case, agree priorities and decision rights with two functional managers and write the team's RACI and escalation path.
days.deliverable: Priority agreement, RACI and escalation path
checks: Both functional managers agree the team's priorities
The RACI has one accountable owner per decision
The escalation path has levels and time limits

days.topic: Managing Difficult Behaviours: Toxic, Disengaged and High-Ego Performers
subtopics: The cost of tolerating poor behaviour
Protecting the rest of the team
days.lab_task: Hold behaviour conversations with a role-played toxic high performer and a disengaged team member, set clear expectations and consequences, and document both.
days.deliverable: Two conversation plans, recordings and documentation
checks: The conversations describe behaviours, not personalities
Each conversation states expectations and consequences

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Team Health Turnaround Plan
days.lab_task: Diagnose a struggling team in a detailed case, write a ninety-day turnaround plan covering performance, behaviour, safety, development and retention, and present it to a role-played senior leader.
days.deliverable: Diagnosis and ninety-day turnaround plan
checks: The diagnosis uses evidence from the case
The plan has actions, owners and measures for each problem
The senior leader approves the plan or gives specific conditions
objectives: Present a plan to senior leaders

advanced.summary: For senior managers, heads of function and leaders of leaders. Covers leading managers, organisation design, setting direction for a function, leadership presence, designing culture, large-scale transformation, talent strategy and succession, strategic workforce planning, leadership team effectiveness, accountability and decision rights, people analytics, ethical trade-offs, crisis leadership, personal resilience, board relationships, global leadership, innovation, restructuring and redesigning work for AI.
prerequisites: Leads managers or a function of significant size
Has several years of people management experience
Takes part in business planning or leadership team decisions
outcomes: Lead managers and design organisations that deliver strategy
Shape culture, talent and workforce plans for the long term
Lead transformation, crises and restructuring with integrity
Build effective leadership teams and represent the function to boards

days.topic: Leading Leaders: Moving from Managing Work to Managing Managers
subtopics: What changes when your reports are managers
Setting context instead of directing work
Holding managers accountable for their teams
days.lab_task: Review manager effectiveness data for a case function, hold a skip-level meeting and a coaching conversation with a struggling manager, and design your leadership team rhythm.
days.deliverable: Manager review, conversation notes and leadership rhythm
checks: The review identifies the weakest manager practices from data
The conversation ends with development actions
The rhythm includes one-to-ones, team meetings and skip-levels

days.topic: Organisational Design and Spans of Control
subtopics: Functional, product, regional and matrix structures
days.lab_task: Redesign a case function to support a new strategy, compare two structures against scenarios, set spans and layers and write the transition plan.
days.deliverable: Two design options, scenario tests and transition plan
checks: Each design states how it supports the strategy
Both designs are tested against at least three scenarios
The transition plan covers people, timing and risks

days.topic: Setting Direction: Vision, Strategy and Priorities for a Function
subtopics: Strategy as choices about where and how
days.lab_task: Run a strategy workshop with a role-played leadership team, produce a strategy on one page with three priorities and a stop list, and cascade it into team goals.
days.deliverable: Strategy on one page, stop list and cascaded goals
checks: The strategy states what the function will not do
No more than three priorities are set
Each team goal links to a priority

days.topic: Leadership Presence and Communication for Senior Leaders
subtopics: What presence means and how it is perceived
days.lab_task: Deliver a recorded five-minute leadership message under pressure from a challenging audience, review it with 360-style feedback and practise a leadership story.
days.deliverable: Recording, feedback summary and a leadership story
checks: The core message lands in the first minute
The story links an experience to a leadership message

days.topic: Culture by Design: Values, Behaviours and Systems
subtopics: Culture as how work really gets done
Systems that shape culture: hiring, rewards, promotions
days.lab_task: Diagnose the culture of a case organisation, define five target behaviours, audit hiring, reward and promotion systems against them and write a culture change plan.
days.deliverable: Culture diagnosis, behaviour definitions and change plan
checks: The diagnosis uses survey and behavioural evidence
The plan changes at least two people systems

days.topic: Leading Large-Scale Transformation
days.lab_task: Build a transformation roadmap for a case organisation with a case for change, coalition, phases and measures, and present it to a role-played executive committee.
days.deliverable: Transformation roadmap and executive presentation
checks: The case for change uses evidence and urgency
Phases have goals, measures and dependencies
The executive committee approves with clear sponsorship

days.topic: Talent Strategy: Succession, High Potentials and Bench Strength
subtopics: Talent reviews and the nine-box grid
tools: HR system such as Workday or SuccessFactors
days.lab_task: Run a talent review for a case function with the nine-box grid, build succession plans for three critical roles and challenge each other's ratings for bias.
days.deliverable: Talent review outcomes and succession plans
checks: Each person has evidence for their placement
Each critical role has ready-now and ready-later successors
Ratings are challenged and adjusted with reasons

days.topic: Strategic Workforce Planning and Skills for the Future
subtopics: Build, buy, borrow and automate options
days.lab_task: Build a three-year workforce plan for a case function with future skills, a skills gap analysis and build, buy, borrow or automate choices, tested against two scenarios.
days.deliverable: Three-year workforce plan with scenarios
checks: The plan states the strategic needs it supports
The plan is tested against two scenarios

days.topic: Leadership Team Effectiveness: Building the Top Team
subtopics: Trust and conflict at the top
The leader's role in the top team
days.lab_task: Assess a case leadership team, design a one-day offsite agenda that addresses its weakest areas and write a decision protocol for the team.
days.deliverable: Team assessment, offsite design and decision protocol
checks: The assessment identifies the two weakest areas
The agenda addresses both weak areas
The protocol states decision methods and who decides
objectives: Improve trust and decisions at the top

days.topic: Governance, Accountability and Decision Rights in Organisations
subtopics: Why unclear decision rights slow organisations
Decision rights frameworks such as RAPID and RACI
days.lab_task: Map the decision rights and forums of a case function, find the decisions that are slow or unclear, redesign them with a decision rights framework and simplify one forum.
days.deliverable: Governance map and redesigned decision rights
checks: Slow or unclear decisions are identified
Each redesigned decision has one decider
At least one forum is merged or removed

days.topic: Leading with Data: People Analytics and Engagement Surveys
subtopics: Linking people data to business results
Acting on survey results with teams
Privacy and ethics in people data
days.lab_task: Analyse sample engagement, attrition and hiring data for a case function, identify the three most important issues and write an action plan with managers.
days.deliverable: People analytics findings and action plan
checks: Findings are supported by the data
Three issues are chosen with reasons
The plan assigns actions to managers with measures

days.topic: Ethical Leadership and Hard Trade-Offs
subtopics: Values in conflict: profit, people and customers
Speaking up and protecting those who do
Pressure from above to cut corners
Ethics in AI and data use
days.lab_task: Work through three ethical dilemma cases in groups using a decision framework, defend the decisions to a role-played panel and write how you would explain each to staff.
days.deliverable: Three case decisions with explanations
checks: Each decision follows the framework steps
Decisions are defended with reasons against challenge
Staff explanations are honest about the trade-offs

days.topic: Leading Through Crisis and Uncertainty
days.lab_task: Lead a timed crisis simulation for a major outage, set up the crisis team, make three decisions with incomplete information and communicate to staff, customers and leadership.
days.deliverable: Crisis team charter, decision log and communications
checks: The crisis team has roles within the first fifteen minutes
Decisions are logged with information and reasoning
Updates go to all groups on the agreed rhythm

days.topic: Resilience and Renewal for Senior Leaders
subtopics: Energy management: physical, mental and emotional
days.lab_task: Complete an energy audit for a typical month, identify drains and sources of energy, and write a personal renewal plan with boundaries and support you will put in place.
days.deliverable: Energy audit and personal renewal plan
checks: The audit lists drains and sources with examples
The plan names people or resources for support

days.topic: Board and Investor Relationships for Senior Leaders
days.lab_task: Prepare and present a functional update to a mock board, take challenging questions and deliver one piece of bad news with your plan to address it.
days.deliverable: Board update, Q&A preparation and presentation notes
checks: The update states performance, risks and asks
Questions are answered directly and briefly
The bad news is clear and paired with a plan

days.topic: Global Leadership Across Cultures
subtopics: Decision making and hierarchy across cultures
Global and local balance in decisions
days.lab_task: Lead a case global team with members in four countries, diagnose a cultural misunderstanding, adapt your feedback approach and write a global team charter.
days.deliverable: Diagnosis, adapted feedback plan and global team charter
checks: The diagnosis names the cultural differences involved
Feedback plans differ by culture with reasons
The charter addresses time zones and decision making

days.topic: Leading Innovation and Experimentation
subtopics: Protecting new ideas from the core business
days.lab_task: Build an innovation portfolio for a case function, design two experiments with success criteria and a budget, and define how successful experiments will scale.
days.deliverable: Innovation portfolio, experiment designs and scaling criteria
checks: The portfolio mixes core, adjacent and new ideas
Each experiment has a hypothesis and success criteria
Scaling criteria and owners are defined

days.topic: Restructuring and Redundancy: Leading People Through It
days.lab_task: Plan a restructuring in a case function with fair selection criteria, consultation steps and conversation scripts, and role-play the conversation with an affected employee.
days.deliverable: Restructuring plan and conversation recording
checks: The plan includes required consultation steps
Selection criteria are objective and documented
The conversation is clear, respectful and offers support
objectives: Support people who leave and stay
